title: Executive Director, Research Administration Transformation & Operational Excellence
text:
Discover Your Career at Emory University: Emory University is a leading research university that fosters excellence and attracts world-class talent to innovate today and prepare leaders for the future. We welcome candidates who can contribute to the excellence of our academic community. Description:

The Executive Director for Research Administration Transformation & Operational Excellence provides executive strategic and operational leadership for the Office of Research Administration's (ORA) enterprise-wide transformation portfolio.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

* Leads an enterprise-wide transformation portfolio spanning research administration functions across schools, units, and Emory Healthcare, requiring university-wide change leadership and executive influence.
* Partners with Artificial Intelligence & Digital Strategy (AI & DS) to implement a broad portfolio that includes enterprise technology implementation (including the Insight grants management system), organizational redesign, shared services transformation, operational performance improvement, artificial intelligence and emerging technology strategy, and research administration training and professional development.
* Directs implementation, ongoing maintenance, and optimization of enterprise systems and tools, including Insight and LegalSifter, and ensures that technology investments support the future-state operating model.
* Co-leads implementation and ongoing review of future-state operating model, including organizational design, workflow refinement, shared services transformation, and operational performance.
* Exercises decision-making authority over implementation, configuration alignment, workflow and business process design, user acceptance, vendor management, future-state operating model alignment, and continuous refinement across pre-award, post-award, agreements, effort reporting, personnel, and compliance modules.
* Manages vendor performance (including Huron), monitors project milestones, and reports status, risks, decisions, and outcomes to the Vice President and Steering Committee.
* Holds executive accountability for realization of transformation outcomes, including organizational effectiveness, service excellence, operational efficiency, adoption, and sustained performance improvement.
* Partners with AI & DS to implement technology programs and enabling capabilities required for responsible AI success. This includes project management, development and evaluation of workflows, tool evaluation, implementation, governance, workforce readiness, and adoption. Manages technology evaluation, implementation, and security coordination in partnership with Emory OIT and Information Security.
* Serves as ORA's operational technologies (Insight, SciShield, Huron, etc.) liaison to central technology and governance bodies.
* Provides subject matter expertise to the Learning and Organizational Development team for the design and deployment of a scalable, role-based training ecosystem that includes Insight and Compass system training, process-compliance content, change enablement, and professional development for ORA and school-based research administration staff.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

* Bachelor's degree in business administration, public administration, health administration, or a related field from an accredited institution and eight years of progressively responsible professional experience in related research administration experience, including a minimum of five years of experience in a management role with direct supervisory responsibility.
* Master's degree (MBA, MPA, MHA, MS, or related discipline) strongly preferred.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

* Master's degree or doctoral degree in a relevant field.
* Experience with Huron's Insight platform at an R1 university or academic medical center in a project leadership or system administration capacity.
* Direct, client-side experience supporting or co-leading a management consulting engagement (EY, Huron Consulting, Deloitte, or equivalent) in a research or academic operations context.
* Experience building or leading a training, learning and development, or organizational capability function in a higher education or healthcare research environment.
* Knowledge of AI governance frameworks, responsible AI principles, and federal data security and research security requirements.
* Demonstrated experience with process improvement methodologies (Lean, Six Sigma, Agile, or equivalent); certification preferred.
* Professional certification in one or more of the following: research administration (CRA or CPRA), project management (PMP), or change management (Prosci ADKAR / CCMP).
* Experience in a centralized or shared services research administration environment, particularly at an institution transitioning from a decentralized model.
* Familiarity with Emory University's systems, culture, and governance structure, or comparable experience at an AAU or Carnegie R1 institution.

NOTE: Position tasks are generally required to be performed in-person at an Emory University location. Remote work from home day options may be granted at department discretion. Emory reserves the right to change remote work status with notice to employee.
